name: Daytona (Windows sandboxes)

modes.label: Windows VM sandbox (presets small/medium/large)
modes.note: Pricing page lists 'OS, Windows, $0.0858/vCPU/h' as its own line next to vCPU/Memory/Storage, i.e. a surcharge ADDED to $0.0504 (= $0.1362/vCPU-h). Presets: windows-small 1/4/30, windows-medium 2/8/50, windows-large 4/16/50 (vCPU/GiB/GiB disk). Default: auto-pause after 60 min idle, auto-stop disabled; paused = disk only.

internet.allowlist: Daytona 'essential services': package managers (npm, PyPI, RubyGems...), Git hosts (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure DevOps), AI APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI, Hugging Face +20), cloud platforms (AWS/GCP/Azure), con

evidence.quote: Network access is restricted and cannot be overridden at the sandbox level.
Full internet access is available by default.

plans.name: Tier 1 (email verified)
plans.note: Tier table says 10 GiB RAM, the limits table on the same page says 20 GiB. 30 GiB disk pool: a windows-large (50 GiB disk) cannot start; at most 1 windows-small (30 GiB disk). Egress restricted (essential services only).

plans.name: Tier 2 (card + $25 top-up)
plans.note: One-time $25 prepaid top-up spent as credit. The 300 GiB disk pool allows 6 running windows-large/medium (50 GiB each); RAM allows 12 windows-large. Egress restricted.

plans.name: Tier 3 ($500 top-up)
plans.note: One-time $500 prepaid top-up. 31 windows-large (RAM-bound) / 40 windows-medium (disk-bound, 2000/50) concurrently. Full internet.

plans.name: Tier 4 ($2,000 top-up every 30 days)
plans.note: Needed above Tier 3 pool (250 vCPU / 500 GiB).

caveats: Windows surcharge encoded as ADDITIVE ($0.0504 + $0.0858 = $0.1362/vCPU-h) per the live pricing page layout; cards/daytona.json 'windows' mode still encodes it as a replacement ($0.0354 extra). If the replacement reading is right this card is ~$0.14/h too high for windows-large.
Only presets with fixed 4 GiB/vCPU: a 4 vCPU / 8 GiB need is priced as windows-large (16 GiB).
60-minute idle auto-pause tail billed at full rate; disk billed while paused/stopped (no archive for VMs).
Tier 1 and Tier 2 orgs have restricted egress that cannot be overridden (essential services only); full internet needs the Tier 3 $500 top-up.
Creating/Starting/Stopping/Pausing transitions are billed as Started; snapshots created from a sandbox remain billed for storage at an unpublished rate.

fleet.verification: Tier 1: verified email. Tier 2: linked credit card and $25 top-up. Tier 3: $500 top-up. Tier 4: $2,000 every 30 days.
fleet.tiers: Default-region pools (vCPU/RAM/disk): T1 10/10 (or 20)/30; T2 100/200/300; T3 250/500/2000; T4 500/1000/5000. Windows presets hit the RAM and disk pools first (4 GiB/vCPU, 30-50 GiB disk each; running sandboxes hold disk quota, stopped/paused VMs release it). Max concurrent windows-large per tier: T1 0 (30 GiB disk < 50), T2 6 (disk-bound), T3 31 (RAM-bound), T4 62 (RAM-bound). Windows-small on T1: 1 (30 GiB disk). More needs custom limits via support@daytona.io.
fleet.notes: Windows shares organization resource quotas. No fixed sandbox-count quota. Official page disagrees on Tier-1 RAM (10 GiB in access table, 20 GiB in limits table); verify dashboard. GPU allowance not numerically established.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: if neither auto-pause nor auto-stop is set, non-ephemeral sandbox classes that support pausing default to an auto-pause interval of 60 minutes with auto-stop disabled
snapshot_auto.note: Windows is a VM class that supports pause; idle auto-pause (default 60 min, configurable, 0 disables) preserves filesystem AND memory: 'The filesystem and memory state are preserved, and CPU is no longer consumed.' Resume continues processes. Stop (manual/auto-stop) only preserves the filesystem (offloaded to nearby storage).

snapshot_on_demand.note: Lifecycle matrix: Windows column supports snapshot-from-sandbox cold (fs) and hot (fs+memory, includeMemory=True; SDK method _experimental_create_snapshot) and new Windows sandboxes boot from it; fork of a started Windows sandbox also copies filesystem + memory. Windows snapshots can only be produced this way (no base-image builds). Snapshot storage billed, rate unpublished.

harness_api.quote: Daytona is the default sandbox provider for the Universal Harness API. Brainbase manages the sandbox for you
harness_api.note: No first-party harness API: Claude Code/OpenCode/Codex guides drive agents via generic exec/PTY/SSH; the only harness API is third-party (Brainbase). Guides are Linux-oriented anyway; Windows sandboxes target computer use.

egress_allowlist.quote: Each sandbox runs behind a firewall that restricts which external IP addresses and domains it can reach
egress_allowlist.note: networkAllowList (IPv4 CIDR), domainAllowList (wildcards) or networkBlockAll, set at create or updated live; Tier 1/2 orgs are forcibly restricted (essential services only), custom lists need Tier 3/4. Docs apply it to all sandboxes and do not exclude VM/Windows classes, but no Windows-specific confirmation (hence medium).

egress_http_rules.quote: Implement [domain allow listing](#domain-allow-list-format) on your own proxy to control which destinations the sandbox can reach.
egress_http_rules.note: Firewall params are only CIDR / domain / block-all; outboundProxyUrl chains to YOUR upstream proxy (via HTTP_PROXY env), so any HTTP-level rules are customer-side, not Daytona's.

ingress_rules.quote: If a sandbox has its `public` property set to `true`, preview links are publicly accessible without authentication. Otherwise, authentication is required.
ingress_rules.note: Private-by-default preview URLs with sandbox-wide token (header) or signed per-port expiring revocable URLs; SSH via tokens. No IP allowlists; any port 1-65535 can be previewed (no port selection).

secret_proxy.quote: Secrets are organization-scoped, encrypted credentials that Daytona injects into a sandbox's outbound HTTPS traffic without ever placing the plaintext inside the sandbox.
secret_proxy.note: Arbitrary secrets with per-secret host allowlist; sandbox env var holds placeholder dtn_secret_...; proxy substitutes in HTTPS request headers only (no bodies, query, plain HTTP, Basic-auth-encoded), scrubs responses. No DB/SSH/non-HTTP. Docs are class-agnostic; not confirmed specifically for Windows VMs (needs proxy CA trust in the Windows store) - hence medium.

isolation.quote: Nested virtualization exposes KVM (`/dev/kvm`) inside the guest, so the sandbox can run its own virtual machines with hardware acceleration.
isolation.note: Docs describe VM/Windows sandboxes as 'a full virtual machine' scheduled by a 'runner'; the KVM reference (for the Linux-VM-only nested-virt feature) implies the underlying host hypervisor is KVM/QEMU, but no page names the Windows-guest hypervisor explicitly.

docker_inside.quote: VM sandboxes are distinct from container sandboxes and support VM-only capabilities: ... Nested virtualization (#nested-virtualization) (Linux VM only)
docker_inside.note: Nested virtualization (/dev/kvm, needed for Docker Desktop/WSL2-backed containers on Windows) is documented as Linux-VM-only; no Windows-specific Docker/container support is documented.

anti_bot.quote: Computer Use enables programmatic control of desktop environments within sandboxes. It provides mouse, keyboard, screenshot, screen recording, and display operations for automating GUI interactions and testing desktop applications.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Windows sandboxes are a general-purpose desktop/computer-use VM, not a browser stealth/anti-detection product; no fingerprinting/stealth features are documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Computer Use enables programmatic control of desktop environments within sandboxes.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — no CAPTCHA-solving service is documented anywhere in Daytona's docs.

egress_ip_type.quote: Each sandbox runs behind a firewall that restricts which external IP addresses and domains it can reach
egress_ip_type.note: No residential/mobile IP product is documented; egress runs from Daytona's own cloud infrastructure (standard datacenter IPs). Exact ranges/type not published.

fork_running.quote: Click the three-dot menu (⋮) next to the started Windows sandbox you want to fork ... Forking creates a duplicate of a Windows sandbox's filesystem and memory state in a new sandbox. The forked sandbox is fully independent.
fork_running.note: Fork is performed on a started (running) Windows sandbox without stopping it first; the fork captures filesystem + memory state.

wake_on_request.quote: A sandbox that is stopped and started again gets a new token, and tokens issued before that stop no longer work
wake_on_request.note: not offered: Daytona's docs describe only explicit start()/resume() calls (dashboard, SDK, CLI, API); no doc describes an incoming preview/API request automatically waking a stopped or paused sandbox.

volume_attach.quote: Volumes are FUSE-based mounts that provide shared file access across Daytona sandboxes.
volume_attach.note: Volume-mount examples all use CreateSandboxFromSnapshotParams with a `language` (container/Linux-VM) runtime; FUSE mounts are a Linux kernel mechanism with no documented Windows-guest support, and no Windows example/mention exists in the volumes docs.

volume_shared.quote: a single volume can be mounted to multiple sandboxes
volume_shared.note: Shared-volume mounting is documented, but only for container/Linux-VM sandboxes (FUSE-based); not documented for Windows sandboxes, so treated as not offered for this class.

live_resize.quote: On a running sandbox, you can increase CPU and memory without interruption. To decrease CPU or memory, or to increase disk capacity, stop the sandbox first.
live_resize.note: Resize section is generic (not scoped to container-only); Windows VM sandboxes are otherwise treated identically to Linux VM sandboxes for lifecycle ops (pause/resume, fork, resize), so increase-only live resize is assumed to apply. Not explicitly Windows-confirmed.

own_agent_api.quote: Computer Use provides the programmatic API for AI agents to automate operations.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope — Daytona ships a generic Computer Use API (mouse/keyboard/screenshot) for callers to drive their OWN agent logic; it does not offer a first-party hosted task/browser/research agent of its own.

lang_python.quote: Create a Windows sandbox. ... Select a Windows Snapshot: windows-small, windows-medium, windows-large
lang_python.note: Windows sandboxes boot from a fixed Windows OS snapshot; the `language` parameter and preinstalled Python/Node runtime (process.codeRun) are documented for container and Linux VM snapshots only, with no Windows example or preinstall claim.

lang_node.quote: Create a Windows sandbox. ... Select a Windows Snapshot: windows-small, windows-medium, windows-large
lang_node.note: Same reasoning as lang_python: no documented Node.js preinstall or `language`/code-run support for the Windows sandbox class.

guest_firewall.quote: Each sandbox runs behind a firewall that restricts which external IP addresses and domains it can reach
guest_firewall.note: derived: guest is Windows, not Linux, so nftables/iptables (the field's literal definition) do not apply; Windows Firewall may work inside but this is not documented, and Daytona's own firewalling is enforced at the host/network layer, not proven inside the guest.

static_egress_ip.quote: networkAllowList for IPv4 CIDR ranges ... networkBlockAll to block all outbound traffic ... outboundProxyUrl to route sandbox HTTP(S) traffic through an upstream proxy
static_egress_ip.note: Egress control docs describe allow/deny lists and an outbound proxy, not a dedicated/static outbound IP assigned to the sandbox; no static egress IP product is documented (card also notes egress/IPv4 are unpublished).

eu_data_residency.quote: Regions managed by Daytona and available to all organizations: | United States | `us` | | Europe | `eu` |
eu_data_residency.note: Windows sandboxes are created via the standard create() API which accepts a `target` region, so the EU shared region applies to them as well.

max_session_h.quote: if neither auto-pause nor auto-stop is set, non-ephemeral sandbox classes that support pausing default to an auto-pause interval of 60 minutes with auto-stop disabled
max_session_h.note: No hard maximum runtime is documented; a Windows sandbox keeps running until stopped/paused by auto-stop/auto-pause (user-configurable, including disabling both) or manually — i.e. no fixed session cap analogous to serverless function timeouts.

image_oci.quote: VM sandboxes can currently only be created from existing VM snapshots. Dynamic builds through the declarative builder are supported for container sandboxes only.
image_oci.note: Windows is a VM-class sandbox; custom Docker/OCI image builds only exist for the Container class. Windows sandboxes can only be created from the fixed windows-small/medium/large VM snapshots.

public_ipv4.quote: Daytona provides preview URLs for accessing services running in your sandboxes. Any process listening for HTTP traffic on ports 1 - 65535 can be previewed through a generated URL.
public_ipv4.note: Inbound access is exclusively via generated HTTPS preview URLs (standard/signed, token-authenticated); network-limits.md only describes outbound firewalling (allow lists/CIDR/domain), no public IPv4 assignment or raw TCP endpoint is documented for any sandbox class including Windows.

gpu.quote: Available lifecycle features depend on the sandbox class. | Lifecycle feature | Container | Linux VM | Windows | GPU | ... | Pause / resume sandboxes | ✗ | ✓ | ✓ | ✗ |
gpu.note: GPU is its own separate sandbox class (NVIDIA/AMD, distinct daytona-gpu snapshot) from Windows; the windows-small/medium/large snapshots list no GPU column value, and pricing/limits never pair GPU with Windows presets.

macos.quote: Daytona also provides ... macOS sandboxes running on dedicated Apple silicon hardware.
macos.note: macOS is a distinct sandbox product (own snapshots/dedicated Apple-silicon hardware) separate from the Windows VM class this card models; outside what the Windows product is.

arm64.note: Windows VM presets are only described alongside Windows-on-x86 tooling/workflows; the only ARM hardware Daytona documents is the dedicated Apple-silicon macOS product, a different sandbox class. No ARM64 Windows offering is documented.

self_host.quote: This repository is no longer maintained. As of June 2026, Daytona's core development has moved to a private codebase. This repository will receive no further updates, fixes, or releases.
self_host.note: The only public/self-hostable Daytona codebase is a frozen, unmaintained snapshot whose documented feature set (Sandboxes/Snapshots/Volumes/etc.) never included Windows, GPU, or macOS sandbox classes; current Windows sandboxes run only on Daytona's managed cloud.

open_source.quote: This repository is no longer maintained. As of June 2026, Daytona's core development has moved to a private codebase.
open_source.note: The historical daytonaio/daytona repo was AGPL-3.0, but as of the June 2026 move to a private codebase the live/current Daytona platform (including Windows sandboxes) is not developed in the open; the frozen public repo also never modeled Windows sandboxes.
